entries.name: PointNet
entries.definition: A neural architecture for unordered point clouds that applies shared pointwise feature extraction and symmetric max pooling to produce a global representation, with a per-point prediction extension for segmentation.
entries.identity_notes: This is the original PointNet architecture, including its classification and segmentation paths. It is distinct from PointNet++'s hierarchical local grouping and from a generic set-pooling model.
entries.mechanism: Shared multilayer perceptrons encode points; max pooling aggregates their features. The segmentation path concatenates the global descriptor with point features before shared prediction layers. Learned input and feature transformations provide alignment modules.
entries.locator: Section 4.2, Figure 2 and equations 1–2, PDF pp. 3–4 / printed pp. 654–655
limitations: Permutation invariance of a global output and permutation equivariance of per-point predictions are different properties.
Learned alignment modules do not establish exact invariance to every geometric transformation; no universal accuracy or robustness claim is curated.
entries.title: PointNet: Deep Learning on Point Sets for 3D Classification and Segmentation
entries.mapping_rationale: Shared neural feature extractors, learned transforms and neural prediction paths make this a specific artificial neural architecture.
entries.abstract_interpretation: Proposes direct point-cloud processing with order symmetry for classification and segmentation. The record curates the construction, not the abstract claims of comparative performance or robustness.

entries.name: Set Transformer
entries.definition: A neural encoder-decoder architecture for permutation-invariant set-input prediction that uses attention to encode interactions among elements and learned seed queries to aggregate encoded features.
entries.identity_notes: The Set Transformer is a set-input architecture, not the AIO Transformer Language Model class, an individual multihead attention layer, or the later Set Transformer++ encoder revision.
entries.mechanism: Stack self-attention or induced-attention blocks without positional encoding, then pool encoded features by attention from learned seed vectors. The induced variant first attends from learned inducing points to the input and then from the input to the resulting summaries.
entries.locator: Sections 3.1–3.4, equations 6–16 and Figure 1, PDF pp. 3–4
limitations: The encoder is permutation equivariant; the pooled output is invariant to input ordering. Multiple seed outputs are not input-element labels.
Linear scaling with input-set size concerns a fixed number of inducing points; ordinary self-attention blocks have quadratic interactions. No universal benchmark superiority is asserted.
entries.title: Set Transformer: A Framework for Attention-based Permutation-Invariant Neural Networks
entries.mapping_rationale: The source specifies a learned neural encoder, attention pooling and output network. ArtificialNeuralNetwork is broader without adding a language-model restriction.
entries.abstract_interpretation: Proposes attention-based set encoding and pooling, including an inducing-point route to lower interaction cost. Encoder and decoder operations were inspected before curation.

entries.name: PointNet++
entries.definition: A hierarchical point-set neural architecture that repeatedly samples centroids, groups metric neighborhoods and applies local PointNet feature extraction, with multi-scale or multi-resolution constructions for variable sampling density.
entries.identity_notes: PointNet++ adds hierarchical local set abstraction to PointNet. Multi-scale and multi-resolution grouping are distinct variants within this architecture; the paper also evaluates a single-scale ablation.
entries.mechanism: Farthest-point sampling chooses centroids; neighborhood grouping and local-coordinate PointNet encoders produce features for successive abstraction levels. Multi-scale grouping concatenates features from different radii, while multi-resolution grouping combines lower-level summaries with directly encoded regional points.
limitations: Neighborhood scale, sampling density and the selected grouping variant affect the representation; density-adaptive construction is not a guarantee for arbitrary missing data.
The single-scale ablation, multi-scale grouping and multi-resolution grouping are not identical procedures. No universal benchmark advantage is curated.
entries.title: PointNet++: Deep Hierarchical Feature Learning on Point Sets in a Metric Space
entries.mapping_rationale: Hierarchical learned PointNet modules and prediction layers form a specific artificial neural architecture.
entries.abstract_interpretation: Proposes hierarchical local PointNet extraction and density-aware multi-scale combinations, contrasting global-only pooling. The record retains variant differences without asserting general performance gains.

entries.name: Deep Sets++
entries.definition: A Deep Sets architecture revision whose encoder combines identity residual paths with set normalization while retaining the original aggregation and decoder.
entries.identity_notes: Deep Sets++ is the encoder revision defined by Zhang and colleagues, not an alternate spelling of Deep Sets or a claim that every deeper set network uses this construction.
entries.mechanism: Encoder blocks add an unmodified input to a transformed branch using learned linear maps, ReLU and set normalization. Set normalization uses a mean and variance over each set's elements and feature coordinates, followed by feature-specific scale and bias.
entries.locator: Section 4 opening and Sections 4.1–4.3, Figure 2 and the DS++ block equation, PDF pp. 4–6
limitations: The written standardization assumes a nonzero denominator; this record does not specify numerical handling of degenerate or padded sets.
The change concerns the encoder. Its construction does not guarantee improved training or accuracy for every task.
entries.title: Set Norm and Equivariant Skip Connections: Putting the Deep in Deep Sets
entries.mapping_rationale: The source modifies learned neural encoder blocks with residual paths and normalization; ArtificialNeuralNetwork is the broader architecture class.
entries.abstract_interpretation: Identifies possible training and information-loss problems in deep set architectures, then proposes residual-path and set-normalization revisions. Such failures and improvements are conditional; the paper explicitly does not claim that the original architectures always fail.

entries.name: Set Transformer++
entries.definition: A Set Transformer architecture revision that replaces its induced-attention encoder blocks with set-normalized blocks retaining identity residual paths, while preserving the aggregation and decoder.
entries.identity_notes: Set Transformer++ denotes the specific encoder revision and ISAB++ construction in Zhang and colleagues. It is distinct from the original Set Transformer and from Deep Sets++ despite their shared residual and normalization design principles.
entries.mechanism: The revised encoder uses two successive attention blocks linking learned inducing points and input elements. Set normalization occurs on the transformed attention and feedforward branches, while each residual addition retains its unmodified query-side input.
entries.locator: Section 4 opening and Sections 4.1–4.2 and 4.4, Figure 2 and equations 21–26, PDF pp. 4–6
limitations: This record covers the source's ISAB++ encoder construction, not all possible residual attention variants.
Set standardization assumes a nonzero variance; no universal optimization or benchmark improvement is asserted.
